key_insight: A point-vortex gas can be treated as a Vlasov system, revealing Landau-damping-like phase mixing and strong mode selection in rotating vortex clouds.
engineering_relevance: This kinetic viewpoint helps predict and control collective vortex transport, instability, and coherent structures in geophysical, plasma-like, and superfluid rotation settings.
method: Derive a reduced Klimontovich equation directly on the physical plane from point-vortex Hamiltonian dynamics.
Formulate a Vlasov description with a dielectric-response operator and resonant critical layers.
Analyze smooth vortex distributions to identify damping, quasi-modes, and beam-plasma-like instabilities.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports analytical theory predictions for Gaussian vortex clouds and thin vortex rings, including selective survival of a single quadrupolar mode and excitation of Kelvin modes.
watch_item: The results are theoretical and rely on idealized collisionless point-vortex and smooth-distribution assumptions, so finite-core, dissipative, or noisy effects may alter the predicted mode selection.
paper_title: Landau damping and mode-selective instability of a vortex gas
